title: The Individual Exception
author: Ben Thompson
description: Jensen Huang has been granted an exception from managerial oversight; in the age of AI, he won't be the last.
summary: Listen to this post : Log in to listen Since Thursday: I have created a Sharp Studio service application that manages all of the Sharp Tech studio cameras, lights, mixer, and various other devices. That service can be accessed by a Windows app on the studio PC, an iPhone app, a web app, or an Elgato Stream Deck; every device in the room needed to record an episode is fully remote controlled.
takeaways: The Deflationary Employee The largest company of the 1950s, as measured by market capitalization, was AT&T; in 1959 it had revenue of $7.54 billion and a market cap of $17.1 billion.
In inflation-adjusted terms that’s revenue of $87.5 billion and a market cap of $198.4 billion; we don’t apply inflation to employees.

Or, maybe we do, but in the other direction: what has been striking about the most valuable companies in the world is how their employee numbers have deflated , even as their revenue and market cap have exploded.
